name: CABO 2018-2019 Leaf-Level Spectra v2
reason: Leaf reflectance and transmittance of ~103 species with per-spectrum Latin names. The package uploads reflectance (ref_spec.csv, 3,879 rows), transmittance (trans_spec.csv, 1,971) and absorptance (abs_spec.csv, 1,971) as separate resources with no per-spectrum Measurement Quantity, so the quantity is taken from the resource. ref_spec.csv holds only 1,971 distinct spectra: 1,908 sample_ids were uploaded twice with identical metadata and datapoints (only the EcoSIS _id differs); the repeats are collapsed as duplicates. The 1,971 absorptance spectra are dropped as an unsupported quantity: absorptance (1 - R - T) is derived from the reflectance/transmittance pairs already ingested and is not log10 absorbance. Expected: 1,971 reflectance + 1,971 transmittance.

setup.evidence: Package metadata: Foreoptic Type 'integrating sphere', Light Source 'lamp', SVC HR-1024i: reflectance and transmittance are both integrating-sphere measurements.

name: Fractional Cover Simulated VSWIR Dataset v2
reason: Measured field spectra, not simulated: the package 'contains spectra from six field experiments that measured reflectance and fractional cover', its resource is fractional_cover_no_atmcorr_no_noise.csv (the version without simulated sensor noise or atmospheric-correction artefacts), 1,594 spectra cite their field campaign in reference_for_original_field_spectra, and Dennison et al. (2019) Sec. 2.1 describe in situ ASD field spectra convolved to the 10 nm bandpass. Only resampled ('resampled', 'averaged' processing flags), so not 'simulated' under the format's definition. Each record is named 'GV/NPV/soil field plot'. Category: 'mixture' unless one cover fraction is 1 (48 pure endmembers: vegetation, npv or soil by that fraction). gv/npv/soil fractions, type and use (training/validation) are carried.

name: HyspIRI Airborne Campaign Leaf and Canopy Spectra
reason: Identity-bearing leaf/canopy reflectance and transmittance of ~35-48 materials (crops, trees, soils, NPV) with per-spectrum common names. The transmittance spectra are ordinary unit-scale leaf transmittance (NIR median 0.37; 90th percentile < 0.52 for all 358), not a different quantity or scale: their extreme values (-1,369 to 496) sit at the detector edges (<450 nm, >2300 nm) and in the water bands where transmitted signal is ~0 and the ratio is noise; those bands are masked as NaN. One transmittance spectrum is a failed measurement and is dropped. Per-spectrum 'Measurement Units' = 'Ratio' is authoritative for the unit scale. 30 spectra repeat an earlier spectrum's datapoints exactly (22 with identical metadata, 8 pairs uploaded under two different sample names/dates); duplicates are collapsed on datapoints, keeping the lowest-ranked id and listing the others in duplicate_ids. Soil and NPV spectra carry the Common Name of the crop or stand they were measured in, so they are named from their target type ('soil', 'npv', 'litter') instead. 75 citrus and grape spectra have no Common Name; their 'USDA Symbol' field holds a common name instead of a symbol ('Grape', 'Orange', 'MandarinOrange'), which names them ('grape', 'orange', 'mandarin orange') instead of their spectrum labels or target type; such a value is kept as extra.source_plant_code, not extra.usda_symbol.

drop_spectra.5f5f65ebd338eaf7d1f61b77: Failed transmittance measurement (incense cedar): NIR transmittance ~0.0001 (leaf NIR transmittance is ~0.2-0.5), 492 of 2,151 bands outside [0, 1].

setup.evidence: Per-spectrum Acquisition_Method: 'LC' (leaf clip with its lamp) -> biconical; 'IS' (ASD integrating sphere; reflectance and transmittance) -> directional_hemispherical; 'PG' (pistol grip, bare fibre 22 deg), '4deg' and '10deg' (foreoptics) are the package's outdoor sun-lit setups (Light Source 'sun', Venue 'outdoor') -> hemispherical_conical. Per-spectrum 'Instrument' (ASD_FS3, ASD_FS4, SpecEvo_PSM3500) names the spectrometer.

name: NGEE Arctic 2017 Canopy Spectral Reflectance
reason: Arctic canopy reflectance (plus road/gravel and one water target). Per-spectrum identity is mostly weak: Common Name/Latin name is present for 32 spectra (used as the name), Target Type is 'Vegetation' for 479 of 511 and Dominant_Species is -9999 for 467. Unnamed vegetation spectra are named 'arctic tundra canopy'; Dominant_Species USDA codes, where given, become keywords; road/gravel maps to man_made and water to water. The per-spectrum Spectra_Units 'Percent_Reflectance_0_100' is authoritative for the 0-100 scale. Values beyond the masking window occur only as noise in the atmospheric water-absorption bands and at the detector edges and are masked as bad bands (not a different source scale). Three groups (8 rows) repeat identical datapoints under different species (e.g. arctic sweet coltsfoot, stone bramble, wideleaf polargrass and water sedge with different LMA and C:N). Each group is one canopy measurement (same Spectra_Name and UTC time) linked to the trait samples harvested inside its field of view, so one copy is kept, named 'arctic tundra canopy', with the species as keywords, the linked SampleIDs in extra and no sample_id of its own. Every other spectrum's SampleID is its sample_id; USDA symbols go to extra.usda_symbol.

setup.evidence: Package metadata: SVC HR-1024i (serial 2041) with an 8 degree lens (Foreoptic Field of View '8 degrees'), Light Source 'sun', outdoor, handheld; every spectrum comes from Seward_2017_Canopy_Spectral_Reflectance.csv (510 with per-spectrum Foreoptic '8deg', plus one without per-spectrum metadata whose SampleID NGEEArctic_Teller_Plot01_Lichen_8deg_Refl names the same 8 degree setup). Per-spectrum White_Reference_Standard '99AA04-0715-2212-SRT-99-100' is a Labsphere Spectralon target. The package description's leaf-clip measurements are not part of this upload.

name: Leaf level spectra and LMA for a set of trees, forbs, vines and grasses collected in Madison, WI
reason: 43,054 replicate leaf spectra of 10,105 leaves (3, 4 or 6 replicates per leaf id; 17,086 rows are exact within-leaf copies of another replicate) whose only per-spectrum identity is functional_type (tree/forb/vine/grass); no species. A deterministic 200-leaf sample (one replicate spectrum per leaf id) stratified by functional type keeps the functional-type coverage without flooding the library with anonymous replicates. Material is named by functional type. 1,324 rows of lt_psr_spectra.csv (730 after collapsing within-leaf copies) are about 100 times darker than every other spectrum (90th-percentile level below 0.016 against a dataset median of 0.47, with nothing between 0.016 and 0.05): copies already divided by 100. They are dropped by the darkness check before sampling, so a dark copy is never a leaf's sampled replicate.

setup.evidence: Package metadata: Acquisition Method 'contact', Foreoptic Type 'leaf clip', Light Source 'lamp', Measurement Venue 'laboratory'. Three spectrometers; the instrument follows the resource file (lt_asd_spectra.csv ASD FieldSpec 3, lt_psr_spectra.csv Spectral Evolution PSR 3500+, lt_svc_spectra.csv SVC HR-1024i).

name: Multiscale Mapping of Species Diversity Under Changed Land-use Imaging Spectroscopy
reason: 22,889 airborne AisaFenix canopy pixels; the only identity is the per-pixel 'Tree Species' class (mostly genus level, e.g. Acacia). Tree Species becomes the material name and a keyword, and at most 25 pixels per class are kept (deterministic sample). Pixels without a Tree Species are not eligible. Adjacent pixels frequently repeat identical spectra (2,327 in the raw data, an upsampling artefact); duplicates are collapsed on datapoints before sampling. Class labels: 'Zizphus' -> 'Ziziphus', 'Cypress' -> 'Cupressus' (merged with the Cupressus class), 'Crop' -> 'crop canopy'. The codes 'Ficus_p', 'FicusC', 'FicusS' and 'Citrus_p' are not explained in the package metadata or description (which defers to Table 3 of the linked paper) and are kept as-is. One all-zero no-data pixel spectrum, repeated under 14 classes, is dropped as constant fill.

name: Leaf and canopy level detection of Fusarium virguliforme (sudden death syndrome) in soybean
reason: 5,851 soybean disease-trial replicates (leaf ASD and canopy Piccolo spectra) with no per-spectrum material identity beyond the trial design. A deterministic 200-spectrum sample stratified by inoculation status (per-spectrum field 'Inoculation': '0' control / '1' inoculated) is kept; all spectra are soybean (Glycine max) per the package description. The raw upload contains a 190-row fill-down group: leaf spectra dated 20160729, Plant 238, consecutive SampleNumbers (carried, so the rows differ in a label field), all with identical datapoints; every other plant is measured once per date, so the spectrum and the shared Plant/Inoculation labels are a fill-down copy error and the whole group is dropped before sampling.

name: Hyperspectral data for measuring vegetation nutrients and canopy photosynthesis in a salt marsh
reason: Mixed package. Investigated 2026-10-29 via /api/package and spectra pages: 7,000 of the 7,147 'spectra' come from the resources All_PLSR_coefficients_to_model_{N,K,Na,P,NEE,Fe,FA}_*.csv (7 PLSR models x 1,000 bootstrap iterations; per-spectrum keys '', Iteration, Intercept; values span -7,240 to +6,672) - they are PLSR regression coefficients, which the package description says were 'added ... for their potential use to model the same variables with new reflectance data'. They are model output, not measurements, and are excluded. The remaining 147 spectra (resource Nutrients_CSHRS_Salt_Marsh_Categories.csv) are measured Ocean Optics Jaz canopy reflectance, 401-849 nm, unit scale (max 0.50) despite Measurement Units '%', for Spartina alterniflora (48), S. cynosuroides (49) and ecosystem-scale mixed plots (50); they are kept and named from SaltMarsh_Category. Two pairs of measured spectra repeat identical datapoints under different SaltMarsh_Category labels (S. cynosuroides vs ecosystem scale) and are dropped as conflicting duplicates.

setup.evidence: Package metadata: Acquisition Method 'proximal', Foreoptic Type 'bare fiber' / 'cosine diffuser', Light Source 'sun', outdoor, Ocean Optics Jaz on a canopy reflectance sampler.
